predecessors.name: Kingdom of Macedon
predecessors.text: Thrace, the Chersonese and the west Pontic coast, 'the government of Thrace' assigned to Lysimachus at the Partition of Babylon in June 323

successors.name: Seleucid Empire
successors.text: Lysimachus's Asia Minor, 'Lydia, Ionia, Phrygia and the north coast of Asia Minor', taken by Seleucus after Corupedium (February 281): 'Seleucids gain control of Anatolia'

successors.name: Antigonid kingdom (Macedon)
successors.text: Macedon and Thrace, seized by Ptolemy Keraunos in September 281 ('acclaimed king by the army at Lysimachia'), ruled by Keraunos, Meleager, Antipater Etesias and Sosthenes through the Gallic invasion…

ledger.x: June 323: the Partition of Babylon.
June 323 to 306/305: Lysimachus governs in the name of the kings Philip III and Alexander IV (rule 4 tint under the macedonian-empire dossier, which carries the matching pair).
322: Seuthes III meets Lysimachus.
322: the drawn battle ends the fighting; Seuthes keeps the interior around Seuthopolis (founded 'perhaps around 320 BC').

313: 'Seuthes III supported the revolt of Callatis' against Lysimachus 'by allying with other towns and tribes and blocking the passes of Mount Haemus'; 'Lysimachus, who then had to abandon the siege of Callatis when Antigonus I's commander Pausanias came to its aid'.
ledger.cp: Callatis and the west Pontic cities (backed by Antigonus I and Seuthes III)

ledger.x: 313: Seuthes joins the revolt of Callatis.
310: Lysimachus 'finally subdued Callatis in 310 BC'.
ledger.cp: Callatis and the west Pontic cities (backed by Antigonus I and Seuthes III)

ledger.x: 310: Seuthes 'settled for peace with Lysimachus'.
310 to the end of the kingdom: the Odrysian interior as an autonomous dependency (rule 4 tint).

309: Lysimachia founded on the Chersonese (40.583 N, 26.883 E, near Bolayır/Kavakköy, Gelibolu): 'The city was built by Lysimachus in 309 BC, when he was preparing for war with his rivals'; 'Lysimachus no doubt made Lysimachia the capital of his kingdom'.
306/305: 'In 306/305 BC, Lysimachus followed the example of Antigonus and assumed the title of king.'
306/305: from 'Satrapy of Thrace' to 'Kingdom of Lysimachus' as Lysimachus takes the royal title (Diadochi page: the 'year of the kings', 306-304).

302: 'Lysimachus, reinforced by troops from Cassander, crossed over the Hellespont in 302 BC' and campaigned in Asia Minor against Antigonus; the counter-dossier (antigonid-dynasty) carries the matching pair.

c. 302: 'In 302 BC Lysimachus married Amastris', widow of the tyrant of Heraclea Pontica, which brought the city and her foundation Amastris into his sphere. Counterpart is the generic Greek-city-state slug (Heraclea was an independent polis); confidence 2 because the page states the marriage, not an annexation.
301: Ipsus. Antigonus 'was killed in the battle' and his kingdom 'carved up between the victors'.
301: the settlement after Ipsus.

288 (the Lysimachus page says 287; its infobox and the Pyrrhus page 288): 'Lysimachus and Pyrrhus took advantage of Demetrius' unpopularity in Macedonia and drove Demetrius out' of his kingdom; Macedon was divided between the two.
288-285: the shared kingdom.
285 (Lysimachus page; Pyrrhus page 284): 'In 285 BC, Lysimachus expelled Pyrrhus from Macedonia'.
285: Lysimachus sole king of Macedon.
285/4: Lysimachus takes control of Paeonia.
285: Thessaly follows Pyrrhus's Macedon.

February 281 (Lysimachus infobox 'Battle of Corupedium, February 281 BC'; the battle page gives no month): fought 'Near Sardis (modern-day Sart, Manisa, Turkey)', 'Seleucid victory', Lysimachus 'died during the fighting'; 'Seleucids gain control of Anatolia'.
281: the European half.
February 281: Lysimachus's hold on Paeonia ends with his death at Corupedium.
February 281: the kingdom ends with its king at Corupedium; it had no dynasty (Agathocles, the heir, had been executed in 284/283).

wars.name: Lysimachus's Thracian wars (Seuthes III and Callatis)
wars.outcome: Drawn in 322 ('fought each other to a draw'); Callatis's revolt of 313 was broken when Lysimachus 'finally subdued Callatis in 310 BC', and Seuthes 'settled for peace' keeping his autonomy.

wars.name: Fourth War of the Diadochi (Ipsus)
wars.outcome: 'Antigonid defeat': Antigonus killed; Lysimachus 'received Lydia, Ionia, Phrygia and the north coast of Asia Minor'.

wars.name: Getic campaign of Lysimachus
wars.outcome: 'Lysimachus was taken prisoner by Dromichaetes' and released, 'and Lysimachus is said to have given his daughter in marriage': no land changed hands south of the Danube.

wars.name: War against Demetrius in Macedon
wars.outcome: Demetrius driven out and Macedon divided (288/287); Pyrrhus expelled by Lysimachus in 285 (or 284): Lysimachus sole king of Macedon.

wars.name: War of Seleucus and Lysimachus (Corupedium)
wars.outcome: 'Seleucid victory': Lysimachus killed, 'Seleucids gain control of Anatolia'; his European lands fell to Ptolemy Keraunos within the year.

certainty.note: Thrace's interior and the Danube line are Cliopatria's; the pages give only the coast, the Chersonese and the Pontic cities as firmly held, and the Odrysian interior as disputed.
The Asian satrapies' boundaries (toward Bithynia, Seleucid Phrygia and Ptolemaic Caria-Lycia) and the 288-285 partition line in Macedon are approximate.
